lessons.title: Force in Daily Life
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Push and pull is a force; it is used to open or close a door.
  • The greater the force, the greater the change in the motion of an object.
  • A football moves when force is applied to it, and it moves in the direction of the force.
  • The football moves fast when more force is applied and slow when less force is applied.
  • Tools such as hammer, saw, axe and plier are used to make a task easier.

Activity (book p. 108)

Q: Human beings have made great development with the passage of time and the world has completely changed. But even today some tools of the old times are used. Get information about such tools and complete the following table. (S.No, Name of the tool, Use in the past, Use in the present; i. axe, ii, iii, iv)

Ans: Note: This is a research and table-filling activity, so it has no written answer in the book. The book only says that some of the tools of the ancient times are being used even today, and it gives axe as the first example in the table. The uses in the past and in the present are to be found out by the students.

Q: Name any four tools used in your home.

Ans: Note: This is a personal activity and the tools of every home can be different, so there is no fixed answer. The book gives hammer, saw, axe and plier as examples of tools. A tool is a thing which is used to make certain task easier.

Activity (book p. 112)

Q: Ask students time and again to open and close the door. Give them time to observe. How door can be opened and closed with force and how movement of door is affected by applying less or more force.

Ans: Note: This is a practical observation activity, so it has no written answer. The book states the facts to observe: push and pull are used to open or close the door, push and pull is a force, and the greater the force, the greater the change in the motion of an object.

Activity (book p. 113)

Q: Football match observation: i. When does football move?

Ans: The football moves when force is applied to it. The book says push and pull is a force, and when force is applied, static objects can be moved.

Q: ii. In which direction does football move?

Ans: The football moves in the direction in which force is applied to it. The book says that speed and direction of moving objects can be changed when force is applied.

Q: iii. When does it move fast and slow?

Ans: The football moves fast when more force is applied and slow when less force is applied. The book says the speed of a thing depends on the applied force.

Q: iv. How a moving football is stopped?

Ans: A moving football is stopped by applying force to it. The book says that when force is applied, moving objects can be stopped.

Q: v. How can the direction be changed?

Ans: The direction of the football can be changed by applying force in the new direction. The book says that speed and direction of moving objects can be changed when force is applied.

lessons.title: End of Chapter Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A pulley is a simple machine which consists of a rope and a wheel with a rim.
  • A lever is a machine which consists of a rod; the human arm is an example of a lever.
  • A wedge is like an axe, an inclined plane is like a slide, and a screw is like the cover of a bottle.
  • A simple machine helps us by increasing the applied force, increasing the distance of force and changing the direction of force.
  • In ancient times people used bull cart, tonga and tipcart for transportation; modern means are aeroplane, train and car.

Q1. Choose the correct answer. (book p. 114)

Q: i. Weapons of _____ were used in ancient time. (a) plastic (b) copper (c) stone

Ans: stone

Q: ii. To make the work _____ tools are used. (a) easy (b) willingly (c) hard

Ans: easy

Q: iii. A simple machine is called _____ which consists of a rope and a wheel with a rim. (a) wedge (b) pulley (c) inclined plane

Ans: pulley

Q: iv. A machine is called _____ which consists of a rod. (a) lever (b) wheel and axel (c) screw

Ans: lever

Q: v. We use _____ to move heavy bodies up and down. (a) wheel and axel (b) pulley (c) wedge

Ans: pulley

Q: True or False: i. In ancient times, man did everything with hands.

Ans: True

Ans: False

Ans: False

Q: True or False: iv. Cart was used even in ancient times.

Ans: True

Q: True or False: v. Force can move static objects.

Ans: True

Q3. Match column (A) with column (B). (book p. 115)

Ans: Human arm

Q: Match column (A) with column (B): Screw

Ans: Door handle

Q4. Answer the following questions briefly. (book p. 115)

Q: i. How does simple machine help us?

Ans: A simple machine helps us in three ways: it increases the applied force on the things, it increases the distance of force, and it changes the direction of force. With a simple machine, more work is done with less force and more work can be done in less time.

Ans: In ancient times people used bull cart, tonga and tipcart for transportation. They were pulled by humans or animals and they moved very slowly. Today human beings use aeroplane, train and car etc. Powerful engines are used to run them, so modern means of transportation are fast.

Q: iii. Name some tools which were used in ancient times.

Ans: In ancient times man made tools and weapons from stones, wood and bones of animals. The book does not give separate names of the ancient tools; it only tells the materials from which they were made.

Ans: The book gives this example: push and pull are used to open or close the door. Push and pull is a force, and it is used in our daily life in this way.

mcqs.why: An inclined plane is like a slide. A wedge is like an axe, and wheel and axel is like a door handle.

options: increasing the applied force on things
mcqs.why: A simple machine helps us in three ways: it increases the applied force on the things, it increases the distance of force, and it changes the direction of force. More work is done with less force.

mcqs.why: In ancient times people used bull cart, tonga and tipcart for transportation. They were pulled by humans or animals and moved very slowly. Modern means like aeroplane, train and car are fast.

lessons.title: Staying Safe at Home
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Electricity can pass through our body easily because 70% of our body consists of water, so safety measures are necessary with electric instruments.
  • Do not touch electric instruments with wet hands or while standing on a wet floor, and do not touch bare wires.
  • Do not use more than two instruments in one plug, and never put your finger or a metallic thing in a socket.
  • Natural disasters named in the book are flood, earthquake, tsunami, volcano, falling of an ice berg and cyclone.
  • Natural disasters cannot be prevented, but their effects can be minimized.

Activity (book p. 117)

Q: Think how they can be dangerous to us: i. Electric instruments e.g. fridge, iron, computer — Possible Dangers.

Ans: Note: The book does not list the possible dangers of each instrument separately. It only says in general that tools and machines have created dangers and problems for us, and that electricity can pass through our body easily because 70% of our body consists of water. That is why safety measures are necessary while using electric instruments.

Q: ii. Gas instruments e.g. heater, geezer, stove — Possible Dangers.

Ans: Note: The book does not list the possible dangers of gas instruments separately. It only says that it is necessary to take safety measures while using electric and gas instruments, and that disasters can occur due to human activities, carelessness and blunder e.g. blasts, fires and industrial accidents.

Q: iii. Sharp instruments e.g. knives, forks — Possible Dangers.

Ans: Note: The book does not state the possible dangers of sharp instruments. It only lists sharp objects among the things with which there is risk and danger, so no written answer is given in the book text.

Q: iv. Pointed things e.g. pencils, needles etc. — Possible Dangers.

Ans: Note: The book does not state the possible dangers of pointed things. No written answer is given in the book text; the students are asked to think about it themselves.

Q: Students shall prepare charts of possible harms of broken glass and electricity and hang them in the class.

Ans: Note: This is a practical chart-making classroom activity, so it has no written answer. The book lists broken glass among the hazards that students can face at home.

Activity (book p. 118)

Q: Write fire safety measures. (i, ii, iii)

Ans: Note: The book does not give a separate list of fire safety measures. It only says that it is necessary to take safety measures while using electric and gas instruments, and gives these indoor safety measures: don't touch bare wires; don't touch electric instruments with wet hands or standing on wet floor; don't use more than two instruments in one plug; keep away electric instruments from water; switch off button while putting plug into socket; don't use faulty electric instruments; and don't put your finger or metallic thing in socket.

Activity (book p. 120)

Q: Below are given different pictures which show a natural disaster (volcanoes, cyclone, flood, falling of an ice berg, earthquake and Tsunami). Write below each picture, name of natural disaster.

Ans: The six pictures, in order from top-left to bottom-right, are: 1. Flood (water covering the land and houses). 2. Earthquake (cracked ground and fallen buildings). 3. Tsunami (a very big sea wave coming over the land). 4. Volcano (the erupting mountain). 5. Falling of an ice berg (the big mass of ice). 6. Cyclone (the storm bending the trees). The book says natural disasters can't be prevented but their effects can be minimized.

mcqs.q: A small child is playing with pieces of broken glass on the floor. What should be done?
options: Give the child more glass pieces
Hide the glass under the bed
Keep the child away from the broken glass and inform parents or teachers
mcqs.why: Broken glass is one of the hazards at home named in the book, so the child should be kept away from it. The book also says that if you feel danger, inform your parents or teachers immediately.

mcqs.q: Many tangled wires and plugs are joined to one socket. Why is this wrong?
options: We should not use more than two instruments in one plug
mcqs.why: The book says: don't use more than two instruments in one plug. Joining many instruments to one plug is unsafe.

mcqs.q: If you feel danger, you should immediately _____.
mcqs.why: The book says that if you feel danger, inform your parents or teachers immediately.

mcqs.q: In accidents, we should _____ others.
mcqs.why: The completed statement in the book is: 'Do help others in accidents.' During disasters we should also take care of others.
